clue.text: Disallow pro bridge player's action

parts.note: to be pro something is to be for it
a bridge player makes a bid in the auction

explanation.surface: A rule banning some move a professional bridge player makes at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional player; it is the preposition meaning in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow something is to prohibit it, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Top athlete's main ploy when running

indicators.note: something running is in motion and not fixed, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A star runner's chief tactic during a race.
explanation.definitionFit: An Olympian is a competitor at the Olympic Games, so by extension an athlete of the very highest standard.

clue.text: Live outside a calm old prison

indicators.note: one word sits outside the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
A plus STILL, meaning calm

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay serenely outside some historic jail.
explanation.walkthrough: BE is split around A STILL. The Bastille was the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was a fortress in Paris used as a state prison until it was stormed at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Try aiding unfortunate VIP

indicators.note: an unfortunate result has gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to attempt helping a celebrity who has had bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dignitary is a person of high official rank, which is what a very important person is.

clue.text: A lovey-dovey person with no name wearing nice perfume?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: having no name means that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a soppy, sentimental person in love
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A soppy anonymous suitor dabbed in something sweet-smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop N from ROMANTIC and put A in front. The question mark flags that the definition is an example of being fragrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means having a pleasant, noticeable smell, which a person wearing a nice scent would have.

clue.text: People not keen on Charles and Camilla's Christmas — nation getting upset

definitions.text: People not keen on Charles and Camilla

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The royal couple's festive season leaves the country out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition ends at 'Camilla'; the 's that follows starts the wordplay. Charles and Camilla are Britain's King and Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimonarchists oppose the institution of monarchy, so they are unenthusiastic about the reigning king and queen.

clue.text: Dull home with grand floor cover

parts.note: a matt finish is dull, not glossy
to be home is to be in
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A boring house that has an impressive carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Matting is coarse woven material laid on floors, a kind of floor covering.

clue.text: Fish containing bone left in court

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a tuna is a fish
a rib is a bone
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A fish with a bone still in it, abandoned in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' could suggest wooing or a tennis court; here it is a judicial body.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body set up to judge disputes, a kind of court.

clue.text: Yours truly cutting a lilac, possibly, or flowering shrub

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of these letters
cutting into something means going inside it, splitting it

parts.note: the letters of a lilac rearranged
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A gardener pruning a lilac, or some other blooming bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lilac' tempts as the definition, but it is anagram fodder; the shrub is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is an evergreen shrub grown for its showy rose-like flowers.

clue.text: Sense group rowing must embrace agreement

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something in one's arms, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Common sense says a rowing crew has to accept a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sense' reads as good judgement, but it is one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, one of the five senses.

clue.text: Navratilova triumphantly displays a bit of heart

indicators.note: the phrase displays, or shows within itself, the run of letters wanted

parts.note: inside the joined words, spanning both

explanation.surface: The tennis champion shows real passion in her triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Martina Navratilova was a great tennis champion; her name ends the letters and the next word supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Each atrium is one of the two upper chambers of the heart, so it is part of that organ.

clue.text: Henman perhaps is grabbed by old leader's positive attitude?

indicators.note: being grabbed means being held, so these letters sit inside another word

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the Prime Minister is the national leader
Tim Henman, the British tennis player, is one Tim
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis player clutched by a former premier shows upbeat thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Henman was a British tennis star famed for raising, then dashing, home hopes at Wimbledon, hence the question mark on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimism is hopefulness about the future, which is a positive outlook.

clue.text: Artist's unable to ignore odd parts in religious practice

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and so on of these letters

explanation.surface: A painter who cannot overlook strange bits of a church ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads 'Artist's unable' and 'to ignore odd parts'; the second word belongs to the fodder, not the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a set sequence of actions performed in a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Heading for library, gaining knowledge

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of library
earning means gaining money

explanation.surface: Off to the library to pick up information.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is knowledge acquired by study, as in a person of great learning.

clue.text: Near urban area, bagging good piece of lingerie

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: bagging something means putting it in a bag, so it goes inside

parts.note: a town is an urban area
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Somebody near the town picking up a nice item of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside TOWN, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is a loose garment worn in bed, sold among lingerie.

clue.text: Wanting diamonds, epic poet wagered money

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: Dante wrote the epic poem the Divine Comedy
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: Desperate for jewels, a poet of epics placed a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' reads as desiring, but here it means without.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player puts into the pot before the deal.

clue.text: Item that's made in cafe — tart made differently

indicators.note: made differently means put together in another way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pastry baked in a coffee shop with a new recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human hands, as opposed to a natural one.

clue.text: Unwell American goes after wrong food in Tijuana?

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
unwell means ill
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A sick American visitor blames some bad Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT comes first because 'goes after' puts the ill American behind it. Tijuana is a Mexican border city, hinting at the cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican bread of maize or wheat, an everyday food in Tijuana.

clue.text: Bishop tucked into beer around Italian island

indicators.note: turned around, the drink is read from the end backwards
tucked into means placed inside something

parts.note: ale is a beer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop downing a beer while somewhere around Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Elba is the island off Tuscany where Napoleon was first exiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is an island in the Tuscan archipelago belonging to Italy.

clue.text: Motivated newspapermen thus editing covers

indicators.note: the words cover, or conceal, the letters wanted inside them

parts.note: the end of the first word, all of the second and start of the third

explanation.surface: Journalists inspired by revising their front pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like newspaper front pages, but it signals letters concealed across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enthused is to be filled with enthusiasm, made eager, so motivated.

clue.text: Couple eating little bit of porridge, say, in Oxbridge event

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
porridge is made of oats, one grain being a little bit

explanation.surface: Two students tucking into a spoonful of porridge at a Varsity occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual rowing contest on the Thames between Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is the yearly rowing match between crews from Oxford and Cambridge, the two universities known together as Oxbridge.

clue.text: Medic with zero information on extremely heavy gas

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of heavy
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the figure zero looks like O
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A doctor with no details about some very heavy gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the rest after the ends of heavy. The joke is that hydrogen is the lightest gas of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is a chemical element that is a colourless gas at room temperature.

clue.text: Difficult to admit referee's assistant in top university

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so a word goes inside another

parts.note: difficult means hard
VAR is the video assistant referee in football

explanation.surface: Getting into an elite university is tough, even for a match official.
explanation.walkthrough: VAR, the video assistant referee, is the replay system that helps football referees.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard is the oldest and among the most prestigious universities in the United States.

clue.text: Complete borders of Ethiopian flag

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Ethiopian
to flag is to tire, grow weary

explanation.surface: A description of the full edging around Ethiopia's national banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is the verb meaning to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole or complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Stolen strong drinks for virtuosi

parts.note: hot goods are stolen ones
shots are small measures of spirits

explanation.surface: Pilfered liquor handed out to star performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotshots are highly skilled, successful people, as virtuosi are in their field.

clue.text: Not in debt, love to invest in an apartment

indicators.note: investing in something puts money into it, so one word goes inside

parts.note: A plus FLAT, an apartment
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Free of debts, someone would love to buy a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay afloat financially is to remain solvent, owing no money you cannot pay.

clue.text: Maybe Alex Ferguson's in bed aboard ship by isle

indicators.note: aboard a vessel means inside it, so one word goes within another

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a cot is a small bed
the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: The football manager is asleep in a cabin on a ferry near an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Alex Ferguson, the long-serving Manchester United manager, was born in Glasgow; 'Maybe' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex Ferguson is a native of Scotland, so he is an example of a man from that country.

clue.text: Talks nonsensically and walks clumsily after tea, we hear

indicators.note: we hear points to how a word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the drink is said the same as the letter's name
to waddle is to walk with short swaying steps like a duck

explanation.surface: Someone babbling and lurching about once teatime is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After tea' puts the letter first; only the drink is a sound-alike, not the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To twaddle is to talk silly rubbish, so twaddles is the present-tense verb for talking nonsensically.

clue.text: Prompts people without clothing to accept clothing, finally

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: nudes are naked figures

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word just before it

parts.note: the last letter of clothing

explanation.surface: A cue to naked people to put on some clothes at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to prod or gently urge someone, so nudges means prompts.
